rules.statement: In a single-page frontend whose URL is its navigation state, give every tabbed view its own route path instead of keeping the selected tab in component state, and make a tab change navigate so that it adds a history entry.
rules.why: Tabs held in component state can't be linked, reloaded or reached with back and forward. That breaks the contract that the address bar is the navigation state.
rules.check: Look for new or changed tab components whose active tab is held in React state (useState or similar) instead of coming from the route, and for tab-change handlers that set local state rather than calling the router's navigate function.

rules.statement: Pass the selected view into a page component as a prop derived from the route, so the page holds no state of its own for which view is selected.
rules.why: Because the address selects the surface, the page shows what the URL says, and a deep link or a reload opens the same view.
rules.check: Look for page or container components that keep their own selected-tab or selected-view state, or that fall back to a default tab even when the route already names one.

rules.statement: Keep peer views of one entity as flat sibling routes at a single depth, rather than nesting a second level of tab routes beneath one of them.
rules.why: Nesting adds a second row of tabs for what is a flat set of peers, and gives the route grammar a depth that no other surface has.
rules.check: Look for new routes shaped like /entity/{id}/section/{tab} where the tabs are peers of the existing /entity/{id}/{surface} routes.
